title: TRAK — master checklist

release.native: Regular TRAK Build 470 is available in internal TestFlight; its remaining nutrient issues are not signed off. TRAK Staging Build 34 is available in internal TestFlight. A matching regular-build Android file is prepared; current Android distribution and phone acceptance still need confirmation.
release.backend: Production backend 2715 and staging backend 2714 are live. These are separate environments. Production includes the selected goal, Search and nutrient support plus the coverage-endpoint repair; staging adds the latest Search network diagnostics.
release.next: Build 34 contains the chart-range, target-marker, weight-unit and calculator-serving fixes on top of Build 33. Coach repairs and subsequent phone-review work remain separate local candidates. Integrate against the latest staging source and complete the relevant phone checks before promoting further changes to regular TRAK.

notes: Public, read-only project status. No login needed.
Historical checks are retained separately; a new regression is not closed by an older sign-off.
Updates appear here after the shared checklist is published. Local edits and chat messages do not update it.
Reconciled through 8 September. Released changes, local fixes and reported phone results are tracked separately. This board update does not release a TRAK app build.

changes.text: The maintenance investigation reproduced all 34 journeys and traced the 14 small lower-range misses to the transition into maintenance and gradual corrections. Longer observation improved the count but did not resolve all misses. A range-only change made results worse and was removed; no app release occurred.

Sol completed the goal-history repair and the expanded post-goal simulation, with independent review. Plan transitions passed, maintenance outcomes still need investigation, and the selected maintenance range differs from the current adjustment trigger. These Coach changes remain local; full sign-off is open.

Staging Build 34 is available in internal TestFlight with the All-range, target-marker, weight-unit and calculator-serving fixes, retaining Build 33 Search diagnostics. Phone acceptance remains open. Coach repairs and repeat-check-in controls are not in Build 34.

Coach completion investigation found and verified earlier goal-completion work. The outcome simulation omits choosing a next plan; its existing failed score remains visible. A separate earlier-history edge case is recorded, and Coach test controls are explicitly excluded from Build 34.

Staging Build 33 is available in internal TestFlight with staging backend 2714. The Mac restart cleared the packaging blocker. The build retains earlier nutrient-range retry work and adds Search connection diagnostics; the VPN stall is still open.

The next staging candidate has local fixes for the short-history All range, faint target markers and shared body-weight unit conversion. Calculator serving memory is also tested locally and handed over for integration. These changes are not in Build 33.
Reconciled this shared board with release records, current work and issues since 3 September. Historical sign-offs remain historical; pending phone checks were not marked complete.

Coach review, target-consistency and personal-minimum repairs are implemented locally, with staging controls to repeat a check-in immediately. The broader outcome comparison still fails its improvement gate; staging/backend release and phone acceptance remain open.

The catalogue audit found successful nightly maintenance but unreliable recent grocery triggers and no established daily full-source OFF/USDA sync. Source freshness and reliable completion records are now explicit tasks.

Recent flagged-food catalogue repairs were verified live, including a later per-burger correction. The broader all-region evidence safeguard remains local, and AI model comparisons need reproducible unseen evaluation.

Regular Builds 469/470 and production backend 2714 delivered the selected goal, nutrient, Search and Health work. Build 470 corrected the native feature default; backend 2715 then repaired the production coverage endpoint. Phone acceptance and separate nutrient defects remain open.

Staging Build 28 introduced native Search transport work. A whole-egg query through a USA VPN later stalled despite a quick server response; subsequent uncached food checks were quick. The extreme delay was not fully explained.

Staging Builds 29/30 added nutrient presentation changes and weight units before named food portions. Later range fixes addressed response ordering and retries, but phone testing still found the short-history 1Y-to-All case.

Reviewed backend security work was deployed and retained by the selected production release. A separate signed-artifact promotion gate was added locally; internal distribution is not public-store acceptance.

Staging Builds 21–27 advanced cold nutrient loading, Search speed and diagnostic work while retaining prior changes. The early Build 22 backend pairing gap was resolved. Later phone findings drove further fixes rather than closing the whole feature.

Staging Builds 16–20 added current-goal weight/rate editing, target cards and further food-editor and nutrient corrections. The post-Build-468 review also addressed View all, serving layout, stale projections and recurring-add first paint.

The later Build 468 backend work corrected secondary daily totals, pinned private-food identity and food/recipe projections. Those implementation changes supersede earlier plan-only entries, while cross-surface phone acceptance remains separate.

Aadam confirmed on iPhone that, after hard-closing TRAK Staging Build 15, reopening it and searching immediately, personal and database results showed right away. This accepts the cold first typed-Search case only. Five-second visual stability, View all, repeat-cache, worldwide, recipe, portion and nutrient checks remain open; regular TRAK and production were not changed.

TRAK Staging Build 15 is available to internal iOS testers, with a matching signed Android file ready for manual Firebase upload. It adds compact first-page catalogue Search, explicit View all loading, a bounded per-account exact-query cache and stable personal sections while retaining the existing staging nutrient and Raw Chicken work. Automated checks are recorded privately; phone acceptance remains open and production was not changed.

Staging Build 14 failed two new phone checks: catalogue and TRAK Custom results lagged behind local results, and Raw Chicken had no portion chips. The staging Fast index had not been enabled and the Custom Search response omitted reviewed source metadata. A backend-only correction is now healthy on staging and passes live timing and payload checks; the same installed staging app still needs phone acceptance. Production was not changed.

TRAK Staging Build 14 is available to internal testers. It combines the existing Cronometer nutrient work with the Search first-paint and stable-results correction, shared recipe servings and preserved AI recipe identity. The combined staging backend is healthy. Regular TRAK and production were not changed.

Installed regular Build 467 remains affected: a cold chicken breast Search took about two seconds, Previously logged and My foods could continue appearing afterward, and a recently logged recipe could lose its named serving and show grams. Staging Build 14 is the candidate correction, not a verified-live fix.

The food-projection audit now has an executable source-of-truth matrix, identical cross-path fixtures and parity tests. It confirmed that some secondary calorie consumers still bypass the canonical entries-versus-food-log daily-total rule; that remediation remains separate and open.

Build 464 is installed on iPhone and partially failed phone acceptance: the first Search open after updating still waited for Suggested and Recents; Food Editor changed shape after opening and did not update the Nutrition basis from the TRAK number pad; safe logout used a centred dialog; and Delete Undo waited for sync. Stay signed in passed. Local follow-up corrections are tested but are not in Build 464.

Typed Search was separately reported slow again on Build 464. No exact query or Fast-versus-Full timing has been captured, so this remains an open diagnosis and is not claimed fixed by the empty-Search shelf correction.

Build 464 was built and signed locally for iOS and Android from one tested source. It includes the Search and recurring cold-open corrections, exact serving-choice retention for pending or offline logs, and refined iPhone inactive-state diagnostics. It was subsequently uploaded to TestFlight and installed on iPhone; its partial phone results are recorded above.

The Build 463 missing-Recents issue is corrected in the live backend. Suggested habits no longer block recent non-habit foods from the current meal, and the shelves cannot duplicate a card. No new phone build is needed; close and reopen Search to verify.

New Search issue confirmed after installing Build 463: Suggested can appear while the Recents shelf is absent. Recents are currently narrowed to the clock slot, and their meal-period fallback is blocked whenever Suggested has a card.

Build 463 is valid in TRAK's internal TestFlight group and is now installed on iPhone. Its backend and database companion are live. The matching Android build is signed and Aadam is uploading it to Firebase. Recurring-transition and food-editor acceptance remain open.

Recurring transitions and the serving/unit/icon editor are implemented, combined and reviewed locally. Final tests pass: 3,717 native, 108 legacy-login and 630 backend tests. The three final review defects are repaired; one minor empty-panel metadata follow-up remains. Backend/schema release, a new phone build and device checks are still required. Not in Build 462.

Build 462 is available in TestFlight for internal testers; Apple processing and beta availability are verified. The matching Android file is ready for Firebase. Installation and phone acceptance remain open.

Main coordination checkpoint saved for a pause. Build 462 files and release notes are preserved. Resume with delivery and phone checks, address any remaining regression, then serving-size editing. Other work owners are unchanged.

Build 462 signed iPhone and Android files are ready and release tests pass. Includes Search opening, saved-library visibility, recurring refresh and safe logout. Upload, installation and phone acceptance remain; these issues are not marked resolved.
Search opening: a local native correction removes a disk-cache wait that can hold ready Suggested/Recents cards. A new phone build and timing check remain; the wider idle freeze is not closed.
Reconciled the latest handoff: copy work is paused; reference-food publication and source-inventory review remain open.
Published the shared, no-login master checklist with current issues, unreleased fixes and earlier sign-offs separated.
Deployed the upcoming-slot recurring correction; phone acceptance remains.
Search History and recurring additions confirmed working on phone.
Library filtering, recurring return refresh and safe logout corrected in the unreleased native candidate.

tasks.nextStep: On the current staging build, verify Stay and Discard with disposable data, then failed-sync recovery and account changes. Repeat on Android using the matching release.

tasks.title: Recurring foods refresh promptly after reopening
tasks.summary: The earlier two-minute return delay has a separately tested reconciliation correction. Later release work retains recurring refresh protections, but the exact current-phone hard-close sequence is not signed off.
tasks.nextStep: On Staging Build 33, hard-close and reopen before and after a scheduled time. Confirm the planned card becomes the logged card and calorie total together. Capture any delay, including slow or offline recovery.

tasks.title: Recurring cards transition without duplicates or gaps
tasks.summary: Later regular and staging releases retain duplicate, refresh-race, add/delete and card-transition protections. Full combined iPhone and Android acceptance is still open.
tasks.nextStep: On the current staging build, test scheduled logging, Log all today and on a future day, overlapping entries, template deletion and removal during refresh. Check one card and one calorie contribution per occurrence.

tasks.title: Edit a database food’s serving size

tasks.nextStep: On Staging Build 33, confirm Edit opens promptly with the correct name, icon and Serving card. Change amount and unit; check Nutrition, Review, save/reopen, supported units, dark mode and larger text.

tasks.title: Delete Undo appears without waiting for sync
tasks.summary: The local-admission correction is retained in the later release lines. The previous delayed Undo report remains a required reconnect phone check rather than an assumed pass.
tasks.nextStep: On Staging Build 33, reconnect and immediately delete a disposable food. Undo should appear promptly, restore once and remain correct if sync fails.

tasks.title: Night-shift and custom day-boundary logging

tasks.nextStep: Design logging, offline replay, targets and Health together.

tasks.summary: The native subscription approach has not been selected or implemented.
tasks.nextStep: Compare web and store billing, account entitlements, cancellation and restore behavior.

tasks.title: App-wide copy review — paused

tasks.title: TRAK Custom reference-food publication
tasks.summary: The selected TRAK Custom nutrient support and native presentation were promoted through regular Builds 469/470 and backend 2714. This does not establish that every staged reference-food row was copied to production. Approved catalogue rows, coverage, source visibility and phone acceptance remain separate checks.
tasks.nextStep: Reconcile the approved reference-food inventory in each environment. Check the TRAK Custom shelf, nutrient data and source settings on regular Build 470 and current staging; keep unknown nutrient values unknown.

tasks.title: Raw Chicken Breast shows household portion chips
tasks.summary: The reviewed-source eligibility correction is included in later backend work, and Staging Build 30 added weight-units-first ordering. The exact Raw Chicken portion and calorie phone check still needs a recorded pass.
tasks.nextStep: On Staging Build 33, open Raw Chicken Breast and check that its named portions appear after g, oz and lb, with correct gram and nutrition scaling.

tasks.title: Food-source coverage review needs reconciliation
tasks.summary: A source-access assessment missed datasets already held locally. The assessment was corrected, but worldwide source exhaustion has not been established. This is a research/review issue, not a new phone regression.
tasks.nextStep: Reconcile existing source versions, nutrient coverage and recorded permissions before claiming remaining gaps cannot be filled. No automatic food or database changes.

tasks.title: Edit the current goal weight and loss rate
tasks.summary: The new goal-weight step, review summary and shared current-goal update were delivered through the later staging builds and selected regular release. Goal and daily-target cards use the saved rate without restarting the journey. Phone acceptance across all consumers remains open.
tasks.nextStep: Change target weight and rate, confirm the review screen, then check Coach, Insights, milestones, predictions and daily targets after reopening. Test both lb and kg.

tasks.title: Weight units stay consistent across goal editing
tasks.summary: Staging Build 34 consolidates goal-edit and onboarding conversions through the shared weight-unit module. Local checks cover edit values, saved targets, weekly rates, repeated lb/kg switching and cold reopening. Further phone-review work remains separate; stone is unsupported.
tasks.nextStep: The staging owner must track any later phone findings separately and verify lb/kg input, display, save and reopen without drift.

tasks.title: New Health weights appear without manual syncing
tasks.summary: A foreground pickup correction is included in regular Builds 469/470. It rechecks for a scale measurement published after the first Health read or after returning to TRAK. Automated Apple Health and Health Connect tests cover outgoing weight/nutrition writes too; physical provider acceptance remains open.
tasks.nextStep: Publish a new scale weight while TRAK is open, then test a short app switch and return. Confirm one imported weight and verify manual food/weight writes still appear once in Apple Health or Health Connect. Confirm the intended staging source before testing there.

tasks.title: Import Health changes while TRAK is fully closed
tasks.summary: The foreground pickup correction does not provide continuous import while the app is killed. Background delivery needs its own platform design and testing.
tasks.nextStep: Scope iOS and Android background delivery separately, including permissions, battery limits, account safety and duplicate prevention.

tasks.title: Roll-On staging behaviour and minimum targets
tasks.summary: Roll-On was reported to fail in staging while regular TRAK worked; that report has no recorded final phone pass. The separate Coach candidate also removes a hidden minimum and uses the shared personal minimum, including cache and missing-profile handling. Those newer changes are not released.
tasks.nextStep: Reproduce the staging report with the exact day and action. After integrating the Coach candidate, verify allocation, Why details, incomplete profiles, changed minimums and preserved historical targets without changing redistribution rules.

tasks.title: Coach weekly check-in shows and applies the correct calories
tasks.summary: The reported zero-calorie first plan and incorrect 1,500-calorie repeat led to a local repair of review creation, refresh and acceptance. It keeps one review per period and applies exactly the displayed current targets. Backend and app tests pass, but the fix is not deployed or in a distributed staging build.
tasks.nextStep: The Coach owner must integrate with the latest staging app and matching backend, then repeat the original first-check-in, redo, reopen and accept flows. Confirm all screens use the same saved calories and macros.

tasks.title: Use the agreed personal calorie minimum everywhere
tasks.summary: The agreed height/weight-based Standard minimum and optional Low setting are implemented locally across Coach, goal setup and Roll-On. Existing explicit user choices are preserved, and missing profile details are handled explicitly. The change is not released; the TDEE calculation was not retuned.
tasks.nextStep: Validate Standard and Low with representative profiles and confirm every target surface uses the same minimum. Complete the Coach staging release and phone checks before regular rollout.

tasks.title: Test Coach check-ins without waiting a week
tasks.summary: Repeat check-in and Next test week are implemented with the separate Coach repair. They are not included in Build 34 and are not deployed or enabled. They await a later Coach staging release; the controls preserve accepted history and keep production unchanged.
tasks.nextStep: Integrate with the latest staging source, verify the combined app and matching backend, then enable only in that Coach staging release. Test repeat, advance, retries and account boundaries.

tasks.title: Complete the full Coach effectiveness review
tasks.summary: The 34 maintenance journeys were replayed exactly. All 14 misses followed weight loss and finished only 0.02–0.42 lb below the selected range. Maintenance began near its lower edge, with calories slightly below simulated needs and gradual corrections. The existing Coach had 20/34 inside at eight weeks and 25/34 at sixteen weeks; the original eight-week failure remains. All 68 eligible plan-transition checks and 34 new-goal attainments remain recorded. Comparison-user post-goal outcomes are still unmeasured.
tasks.nextStep: The Coach owner must separate maintenance-entry calorie estimation from the gradual correction policy using declared comparisons, including noisy and sparse data, and add the missing post-goal comparison group. A range-only experiment worsened outcomes and was removed. Full effectiveness sign-off and physical staging checks remain open.

tasks.title: Micronutrient details open with the correct complete view
tasks.summary: Successive staging fixes address cold Today data, partial first charts, delayed targets and stale timeframe responses. Build 33 includes the selected-range retry work. The remaining All-range and marker defects are tracked separately, so the whole nutrient feature is not signed off.
tasks.nextStep: On Build 33 and its successor, open Today, History and nutrient details cold and warm, switch ranges rapidly and retry a failed load. Check for partial old data, delayed target changes or layout jumps.

tasks.title: All shows the full recorded nutrient history
tasks.summary: Staging Build 34 contains the correction for 1Y to All remaining stuck at one year when recorded history is shorter. It uses the actual history span and retains Build 33 work. A related regular Build 470 correction remains separate; full phone acceptance is still open.
tasks.nextStep: On Staging Build 34, test repeated 1Y to All switching with less than and more than a year of history, including empty history, without closing the screen.

tasks.title: Nutrient target markers remain visible
tasks.summary: Staging Build 34 restores solid nutrient target markers across standard, overview and History cards. Values and positions are retained, and automated visual tests pass. Phone acceptance remains open.
tasks.nextStep: On Staging Build 34, verify marker visibility in light and dark modes across nutrient card styles while retaining the same targets, positions and ranges.

tasks.title: Nutrient values and spacing match the agreed design
tasks.summary: Staging Builds 29/30 added the agreed numeric presentation and tighter legend-to-Today spacing, retained by Build 33. Further regular Build 470 formatting corrections are local and unreleased. These are presentation changes, not nutrition-data changes.
tasks.nextStep: Check Today, Daily average, History, tooltips, percentages and small positive values on the intended build. Retain stored precision and verify the final regular/staging formatting agrees.

tasks.title: Micronutrient coverage loads in regular TRAK
tasks.summary: Build 470 restored the intended nutrient screen, then production backend 2715 fixed the coverage endpoint that was returning an error because of an environment mismatch. The backend correction is verified live. The full phone experience, including separate chart issues, remains open.
tasks.nextStep: Retry coverage in existing regular Build 470; no new app build is needed for the endpoint repair. Record the phone result and keep any range or marker defect on its own card.

tasks.title: Show weight units before Small, Medium and Large
tasks.summary: Staging Build 30 changed the serving-chip order to g, oz, lb before named portions such as Small, Medium and Large. Build 33 retains it. The change does not alter portion weights or food ranking.
tasks.nextStep: Check several foods with named servings on Build 33, including scroll/overflow behaviour and correct calories after selecting a weight unit or named portion.

tasks.title: Remember the serving set with the pack calculator
tasks.summary: Staging Build 34 includes the fix that saves calculated grams to the account and restores them through Search, Recents, barcode and restart. For example, 500 g divided by four servings reopens at 125 g. Phone acceptance remains open.
tasks.nextStep: On Staging Build 34, test every reopening route, correct calories, manual overrides, existing diary amounts and account switching. A failed save must be reported; cold offline restoration and older web-app preference migration are not included.

tasks.title: Blueberries entered in grams must not become cups
tasks.summary: A separate serving check requires a small gram amount to stay grams rather than being interpreted as a cup count. The new persistence tests preserve 24 g and correctly scaled calories for a food with cup portions. That is local fixture evidence, not an exact live UK/US catalogue or phone sign-off.
tasks.nextStep: Reproduce the exact reported Blueberries entry and route on the next staging candidate. Confirm 24 g stays grams and uses the selected catalogue row’s actual per-100 g nutrition.

tasks.title: Keep imported food sources measurably up to date
tasks.summary: The 7 September audit confirmed selected OFF/USDA imports, but found no implemented daily full-source delta sync. Recent row additions and local corrections do not prove that an entire source is fresh. Nightly housekeeping is a separate process.
tasks.nextStep: Define source versions, refresh dates and guarded update rules. Preview differences and preserve reviewed corrections before importing changes; track completion rather than inferring freshness from row timestamps.

tasks.title: Restore reliable grocery refreshes
tasks.summary: Nightly catalogue maintenance completed through the audit date, but recent grocery triggers failed before running and the latest successful trigger did not establish refresh completion. Reliable recent grocery results remain unverified.
tasks.nextStep: The operations owner must inspect the last runner outcome and restore scheduling on existing infrastructure, with durable start/completion/failure records and missed-run alerts. No scheduler change was made by the audit.

tasks.title: Evaluate search-engine alternatives after diagnosis
tasks.summary: Typesense, Meilisearch and a managed food API were reviewed as options. No migration is selected. TRAK already maintains an imported catalogue, and the outstanding phone/network delay must be measured before paying to replace search infrastructure.
tasks.nextStep: Compare uncached latency, food-ranking parity, catalogue licensing/freshness and total operating cost only if the measured bottleneck justifies a migration. Preserve current food identification and immediate View all.

tasks.title: Compare Gemini Flash 3.8 across AI features
tasks.summary: The all-feature quality, speed and cost comparison is requested, and prior evaluation suites have been located. Small food-verifier experiments are preliminary and prompt-sensitive; they do not establish a production winner or complete the broader evaluation. No all-feature model switch is approved.
tasks.nextStep: Use fixed current baselines and unseen labelled examples for meal photos, recipe photos/import, label scans, chat and food verification. Count retries and external calls in cost, and report a keep/switch decision per feature.

tasks.title: Recent flagged foods have corrected catalogue servings
tasks.summary: Five recent moderation cases received guarded live catalogue corrections with independent readback. The ASDA reduced-fat burger entry now uses one burger and its label nutrition rather than incorrectly treating those values as per 100 g. Existing diary history was preserved.
tasks.nextStep: Rescan or reselect the corrected products to verify the label serving and calories in the app. Track later catalogue drift separately from the broader unreleased verification-policy change.

tasks.title: Strengthen evidence checks for barcoded foods
tasks.summary: An all-region verification safeguard is implemented and tested locally, separate from the live one-off catalogue repairs. Review, a stale audit assumption about later diary additions, and the final Search cost check remain before backend rollout. No new phone build is required for that backend change.
tasks.nextStep: The food-verification owner must preserve original records while allowing later additions, rerun independent review and Search timing, then complete the separately approved backend rollout and live checks.

tasks.title: Reviewed backend security protections are deployed
tasks.summary: The reviewed September backend protections were deployed and verified, and retained in the subsequent production release. This closes that specific release scope, not every outstanding reliability or security item.
tasks.nextStep: Keep the reviewed protections in future backend changes and track new findings separately. Sensitive implementation details stay in private engineering records.

tasks.title: Verify the actual app before wider release
tasks.summary: A local release gate checks the signed iPhone and Android artifacts and requires recorded phone acceptance for claimed features. Release checks can run on the release Mac. Build 470 remains internal-only; these new protections do not retrospectively approve its unresolved nutrient issues.
tasks.nextStep: The release owner must use the gate for the next candidate, verify matching platform artifacts and collect the required phone acceptance before wider promotion.

tasks.title: Move accepted staging work into regular TRAK safely
tasks.summary: The selected goal, nutrient, Search and Health bundle reached regular Builds 469/470 with matching backend support. Newer staging transport, diagnostics, serving and nutrient follow-ups are separate; Coach also remains unreleased. There is no blanket approval that every staging change is production-ready.
tasks.nextStep: The release owner must reconcile exact accepted changes into the latest regular baseline, preserve concurrent work, pair any required backend first and verify signed artifacts and phone behaviour before promotion.

tasks.title: Goal changes must preserve earlier expenditure history
tasks.summary: The local repair preserves earlier expenditure records when a goal changes on a day without its own saved estimate. It also retains the current adjustment after recalculation. The unchanged independent cases pass on the candidate and still reproduce the old bug on production source. It is not in Build 34; no later release build is assigned.
tasks.nextStep: The Coach owner must retain this repair in the combined staging candidate, verify it with the matching backend, and test goal changes and later recalculation before any production release.

tasks.title: Coach maintenance range matches the selected tolerance
tasks.summary: Coach uses a fixed ±1.5 lb corrective trigger although the user selects a percentage range. A local experiment made the trigger follow that saved range, but reduced eight-week maintenance success from 20/34 to 16/34. It was removed from app code and retained only as diagnostic evidence. The mismatch remains unresolved; this is not a shipped fix.
tasks.nextStep: The Coach owner must resolve the saved-range contract together with maintenance-entry estimation and correction behavior, then validate the combined behavior before staging. Preserve the recorded failed experiment and existing outcome thresholds.
